findings.ACCEPTANCE TEST: Robolectric/instrumented test: searching exact existing brand string returns only entries with that brand; searching exact color returns only that color; package ID returns single entry.
findings.CONSEQUENCE: Users cannot reliably search by exact brand/product/color as required; results may include unrelated items, failing acceptance.
findings.EVIDENCE: MainViewModel.search builds FTS query as each term quoted + '*' (prefix) and only exact package ID via dao.byId(q). No exact equality queries on brand/product/color fields.
findings.FINDING: Search does not provide exact brand/product/color matching; it tokenizes and prefix-matches FTS, which can return irrelevant entries.
findings.REQUIRED CORRECTION: Implement exact field searches (e.g., WHERE brand = :q, product = :q, color_name = :q) or precise FTS phrase matching with field filters.

findings.ACCEPTANCE TEST: Test that a catalog entry with null nozzleMin gets nozzleMin source empty (or 'Missing'), not 'OFD revision'; saving edited record preserves empty source.
findings.CONSEQUENCE: UI displays a source for missing data; edited records may claim catalog provenance for fields never present, violating per-field provenance preservation.
findings.EVIDENCE: CatalogEntry.asCatalogItem() sets all EDITABLE_FIELDS to OFD source regardless of field presence; CustomRecord.asItem() inherits source strings even when value is blank/zero.
findings.FINDING: Per-field provenance is incorrectly assigned to fields with no value, misrepresenting source data.
findings.REQUIRED CORRECTION: Assign source only when a value exists; for missing/null/blank fields use empty source or explicit 'Missing' marker, and preserve this in snapshots.

findings.ACCEPTANCE TEST: Instrumented test with malformed tag fires callback; app shows error and does not crash.
findings.CONSEQUENCE: App crash on invalid NFC tag instead of graceful rejection, violating strict malformed/duplicate/version validation and robustness.
findings.EVIDENCE: MainActivity.onTagDiscovered(tag) = model.nfc.onTag(tag) with no try/catch; core validation may throw on malformed input.
findings.FINDING: NFC tag discovery callback directly invokes model.nfc.onTag without exception handling; a malformed/unsupported tag could crash the app.
findings.REQUIRED CORRECTION: Wrap onTag in try/catch, route exceptions to UI error state (e.g., model.nfcError) and display a notice.

findings.ACCEPTANCE TEST: Create legacy DB with recent for known package, run init, assert recent appears with all fields and provenance.
findings.CONSEQUENCE: Legacy catalog recents may disappear after catalog replacement/removal, contradicting recovery intent; testing gap leaves hydration unverified.
findings.EVIDENCE: restoreLegacyRecent returns null if byId(id) returns null or revision mismatch; StorageAcceptanceTest only tests decodeSnapshot rejection and DB preservation, not actual hydration output.
findings.FINDING: Legacy recent recovery depends on a matching catalog entry and same-generation revision; recents referencing removed/replaced catalog entries are silently dropped, and no test covers successful hydration.
findings.REQUIRED CORRECTION: Either preserve legacy recents as self-contained snapshots (including original values) or document/accept loss; add test that hydrates a legacy recent with matching catalog entry and verifies full item.

findings.ACCEPTANCE TEST: Codebase has no unused catalog generation store in app path; Android storage tests are sole coverage.
findings.CONSEQUENCE: Misleading test coverage; unused code may hide gaps or confuse maintenance.
findings.EVIDENCE: core evidence includes CatalogGenerationStoreTest (2 tests) but no app source reference to CatalogGenerationStore; StorageAcceptanceTest is separate and does not cover it.
findings.FINDING: Unused CatalogGenerationStore remains and its core tests do not exercise Android storage; test suite may give false confidence.
findings.REQUIRED CORRECTION: Remove unused CatalogGenerationStore or add Android storage test that directly validates real database behavior.
